title: Enterprise access-control framework: RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, and periodic access review automation
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Provide a production-ready access control surface that satisfies audit/evidence requirements for enterprise customers and internal compliance: role-based access control (RBAC) at resource and tenant scope, SSO via SAML2 for IdP authentication, SCIM v2 provisioning for user lifecycle, and an automated periodic access review workflow with evidence generation for audits.

Scope:
- RBAC: role definitions, permission matrix for Console and API (models, deployments, billing, logs).
- SSO/SAML: SAML metadata upload, IdP test flow, SAML assertion mappings to roles.
- SCIM: provisioning/deprovisioning pipeline for user/group sync (Okta, Azure AD).
- Periodic access reviews: scheduled reviewer assignments, one-click attestations, automated evidence export (CSV + PDF) and storage to audit-bucket.
- Audit/event plumbing: ensure admin actions and provisioning events are captured with immutable IDs and forwarded to SIEM.

Implementation approach and decisions: 
1) Reuse authsvc as the canonical policy evaluation layer; extend with resource-level role checks to avoid duplicating logic across services.
2) Role model: introduce three axis: role (Viewer/Editor/Admin), scope (Org/Project/Deployment), elevated flags (can_manage_billing, can_manage_models). Roles defined in a YAML schema under infra repo for traceability.
3) SAML: support IdP metadata upload or metadata URL; implement SAML broker in authsvc using go-saml with strict signature and audience checks. Map SAML attributes to groups and then to RBAC roles; provide a test IdP UI for admins.
4) SCIM: implement SCIM v2 endpoints in authsvc; adopt one-way provisioning from IdP to Redwood. For Private deployments allow customer-managed SCIM connector option. Use incremental sync (lastModified) to limit throughput.
5) Periodic reviews: store review tasks in work-queue service (existing scheduler) with configurable cadence. Review flows produce signed attestations (user id, reviewer, timestamp, scope) and an evidence bundle (CSV + PDF) stored in a dedicated audit S3 prefix with retention policy.
6) Audit logs: emit structured audit events on role/grant/SCIM actions with request_id, actor, target, before/after. Pipe to log-forwarder for SIEM and retention.

Trade-offs and risks: 
- SCIM requires IdP configuration from customers and can be brittle; mitigated by step-by-step setup docs and a test connector.
- Fine-grained RBAC increases policy checks cost at runtime; mitigate via in-memory policy cache and evaluation sharding.
- Periodic review automation needs good UX to avoid reviewer fatigue; initial cadence defaults to 90 days and will be tuned.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- RBAC schema and enforcement implemented for Console and API for model/deployment/billing resources.
- SAML SSO flow validated with Okta and Azure AD test accounts.
- SCIM provisioning supports create/update/delete and group sync for Okta.
- Access review flow creates review tasks, collects attestations, and produces evidence bundles accessible to auditors.
- Audit events emitted for all access-control changes and verified in SIEM test index.

Notes and artifacts: 
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/ACCESS-CONTROL-FRAMEWORK (internal design spec).
- SCIM proposal RFC: drive.google.com/drive/folders/SCIM-RFC-2026 (setup examples and payloads).
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authsvc/pull/204 (initial SCIM handlers and SAML broker).
- Compliance checklist: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/compliance/AccessControlChecklist.xlsx

- Complete SAML broker integration tests and create setup wizard in Console (eng + design task).
- Security to run threat-modeling session and sign off (security_review_required).
- Schedule demo with PM & Legal by 2026-03-12.
